items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently observed that the interests of national security must take precedence over personal rights, while restoring the acquistion of land for a Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) AI/ robotics centre [ Defence Research and Development Organisation v. Special Land Acquisition Officer ] . A Division Bench comprising Justice DK Singh and Justice H Shanthi Bhushan on September 21 set aside a 2014 single-judge Bench ruling that had earlier quashed the land acquisition proceedings. The single-judge had reasoned that objections raised by the original landowners had not been properly considered by the relevant authorities during the land acquisition proceedings. The DRDO and the Union government had challenged this ruling by way of appeals, which have now been allowed by the High Court's Division Bench. The Division Bench found that the original landowners’ objections had, in fact, been properly considered and that they failed to show any real prejudice. items.title: SFI moves Delhi High Court over suspension of Instagram account
items.summary: Student’s Federation of India (SFI) has approached the Delhi High Court challenging the alleged delay by the Central government’s grievance appellate committee (GAC) in deciding its appeal against Instagram’s permanent disabling of one its accounts. Justice Amit Mahajan is scheduled to hear the case on September 24. SFI is the student wing of the Communist Party of India (Marxist). According to SFI’s plea, Instagram permanently disabled the SFI Delhi account on July 5, stating that it “may be associated with another account that has gone against our rules” and therefore did not comply with its community standards on account integrity. SFI states that Instagram did not disclose any further particulars or identify the allegedly associated account. The account, created in 2018, had around 13,000 followers. The petitioners said they first appealed the disabling on July 7 and subsequently approached Meta's grievance officer on July 9. However, they received no response, following which they approached the GAC on August 12. items.title: Gujarat HC rejects Ravi Nair’s plea for interim release in Adani defamation case
items.summary: The Gujarat High Court has rejected journalist Ravi Nair’s plea for interim release in a criminal defamation case filed against him by the Adani Group, Bar and Bench reported. The court had earlier given Adani Enterprises additional time to respond to Nair’s petition challenging his custody in a criminal defamation case, pushing the matter to September 23. Justice MK Thakker on Wednesday reserved her decision on Nair’s petition. The court said that it will dictate the order next Wednesday. Nair, a contributor to adaniwatch.org , was convicted of defamation by a Judicial Magistrate First Class in Gandhinagar in February over a series of tweets and articles accusing the Adani Group of corruption, crony capitalism and misuse of government agencies. He was sentenced to a year’s simple imprisonment and fined Rs 5,000. The Sessions Court later suspended his sentence and released him on bail while he appealed the conviction, on conditions including regular court appearances and surrendering his passport. items.summary: The Punjab and Haryana High Court recently sought an explanation from an additional district judge for mistakenly writing that the High Court had stayed proceedings in an application moved by Punjab State Warehousing Corporation for execution of an arbitration award [Hardev Singh and Ors v Punjab State Warehousing Corporation and Anr] The Court was informed that the order staying the operation of the award was actually passed by an additional district judge in Chandigarh who is hearing a challenge against the award. Justice Lapita Banerji called it a serious issue and sought a report from the district judge of Muktsar Sahib. "Let a status report be called from the learned District Judge, Sri Muktsar Sahib, explaining the anomaly that has crept into the order dated August 19, 2026, passed in EXE-86-2024. It is also to be explained how despite recording that the presence of the decree holder is awaited the appearance of the learned counsel for the decree holder is recorded and how after recording that the JDs No. 1 to 7 are proceeded against “ex parte”, the learned ADJ recorded the presence of the learned counsel for JDs No.3 to 6," the Court said.
